steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since {{pt_you}} finished {{pt_your}} aligner treatment with us? Are the teeth still holding straight and {{pt_they_are}} happy with the smile, have you noticed a little shifting starting to creep in, or {{pt_moved_back_q}}?

(This question has only three possible answers. Click the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Holding Straight: Celebrate the Win
steps.content:
I love hearing that, {{contact_first_name}}. That’s the retainer doing exactly what it’s supposed to do, and it means the work {{pt_you}} put in is still paying off. A straight smile that stays straight is the whole goal.

(Celebrate genuinely, then move to the permission ask.)

steps.title: Some Shifting: Normalize, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that’s completely normal. Teeth naturally want to drift back toward where they started, especially when life gets in the way of retainer wear; {{pt_no_fault}}, and it’s exactly why we check in. The good news is that when shifting is caught early, it’s usually much easier to correct.

What do you think made it start creeping back? Was it the retainers wearing out, life getting busy, or something else?

(Let them answer. Do NOT try to book yet.)

steps.title: Moved Back Quite a Bit: Normalize, Then Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that’s completely normal. Teeth naturally want to drift back toward where they started once the retainer routine slips; {{pt_no_fault}}, and it’s exactly why we check in. I remember how great that smile looked when {{pt_you}} finished, {{pt_proud}}.

What do you think made it come back? Was it the retainers wearing out, life getting busy, or something else?

(Let them answer. Do NOT try to book yet. Be warm and non-judgmental.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few quick questions so we get {{pt_your_file}} completely up to date. Teeth are sneaky. They move so slowly you never catch them doing it, so these questions matter more than people think. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes. Almost everyone says yes. You asked permission, and it’s their file.)

steps.title: The Transition: Acknowledge and Ask Permission
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, obviously I know you said you’ve noticed some changes with {{pt_your}} teeth, and we’re absolutely going to talk about that. But while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few additional questions so we get {{pt_your_file}} completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
The Questions: Update the File
Making It Real
steps.content:
(Take the concern they named and make it present with three questions, in order.)

{{pt_mir_q1}}? Since we last spoke, or longer?

{{pt_mir_q2}}?

{{pt_mir_q3}}? (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that, it makes complete sense, and that's exactly the kind of thing we help people with every single day.

steps.title: The Review & Bridge to Emotion
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I've got this right. (Recap what they told you: how long, how often, how it affects them.) Did I get that right?

And it sounds like {{pt_bridge_q}}. Is that fair to say?

(About 95% say yes. That yes is the moment.)

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, a quick scan shows us exactly where the teeth stand compared to where {{pt_you}} finished. If it’s minor, often a refreshed retainer or a short refinement is all it takes to get things back on track, and if everything’s holding better than you think, we’ll tell you that too, because we’re not here to waste your time or your money. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

Based on everything you’ve told me, my recommendation is that we {{pt_get_you_in}} for that quick scan. Does that sound reasonable?

(Ask "does that sound reasonable", never "does that sound good." Click what you hear next.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, help me understand. What's holding you back from letting us {{pt_get_you_in}} to take a look? Is it the timing, or is there something else on your mind?

(Ask this easygoing and curious, not pushy. You're simply trying to understand what's getting in the way so you can help. Then stop and let them tell you.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: Nothing Found: The Retainer Check
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I’m glad everything else is in good shape, and we’re thrilled to hear it.

Let me ask you one last thing. How are the retainers holding up? Still going in at night, or has that kind of fallen out of the routine?

(Let them answer. No judgment either way. Retainer habits slip, and retainers themselves stretch and wear out over time.)

{{contact_first_name}}, even when everything feels like it’s holding, retainers age. They stretch, warp, and wear thin, and teeth will quietly take advantage of that. The easiest way to protect {{pt_invested}} is a quick check: we take a current scan, make sure everything is actually holding where it should, and if the retainers need refreshing we handle it right there. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let’s {{pt_get_you_in}} so we can check those retainers, and that smile stays exactly where it belongs. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Scheduling: Two Yes-Yes Options
steps.content:
Wonderful, {{contact_first_name}}. {{rec_pronoun_cap}} have consultation times available this week on (day) and (day). Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?

(Let them answer.)

Perfect, I have a (time) and a (time) available, which is better?

(Let them answer.)

Great, I've got you down for (day) at (time).

(Always offer two yes-yes options within 48 hours. Before the call, know your two days and two times so you can fill these in without hesitating. Once booked, add your notes and press the green "Scheduled" button below to log the call.)

steps.title: Parent Mode
steps.content: (Parent mode is on, every screen from here uses parent/guardian wording automatically.)

steps.title: Objection: Start all over?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that’s the number one thing people worry about, and here’s the honest answer: usually not. When shifting is caught reasonably early, it’s often a much shorter refinement. A handful of trays, not a whole new treatment. The scan tells us exactly where things stand, and that’s the point of coming in: you’ll know precisely what it would take before deciding anything.

(Do NOT quote specific prices or promise treatment lengths on the call. The scan determines that.)

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for the yes.) Okay, let’s find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: The retainer routine slipped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, please don’t be. There’s truly no judgment here. Teeth naturally want to drift back toward where they started the moment the retainer routine slips. That’s just how teeth behave, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It’s exactly why we check in. I remember how great that smile looked when {{pt_you}} finished, and we’d simply love to help {{pt_them}} protect it.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for the yes.) Okay, let’s find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's the right move, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

The nice thing is, coming in is really just information. You'd find out exactly what the options look like and what it would involve, and then you get to make the decision with real answers instead of wondering. And if it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a link or a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at your specific situation. That's really what the visit is for: you find out exactly what the options look like for you and get answers that apply to you. So let me get you on the schedule first, and you'll have real answers to go on.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?
